example.quest.wolf_hunt.title: Wolves at the Gate
example.quest.wolf_hunt.active: Wolves have been taking sheep from the pastures of Brightwater. The elder is offering a reward to whoever drives them off.
example.quest.wolf_hunt.completed: The pack is broken, and Brightwater's shepherds sleep a little easier.
example.quest.wolf_hunt.log.hunt: The elder's letter spoke of a wolf pack growing bolder by the night. Thinning it out should keep the flocks safe.
example.quest.wolf_hunt.log.report: The wolves are dead. The elder will want to hear of it.
example.dialogue.elder.first_meeting: A stranger in Brightwater? You picked a poor season to visit, traveler. Something has been taking our sheep.
example.dialogue.elder.introduce: I'm only passing through. Maybe I can help.
example.dialogue.elder.letter: Then read this. I wrote down everything we know: where the flocks were taken, and when.
example.dialogue.elder.wolves_pack: A pack, five or six strong. They come down from the ridge after dark.
example.dialogue.elder.wolves_white: Old Tam swears one of them is white as bone. Old Tam also swears his goat can count.
example.dialogue.elder.reported: Truly? Then Brightwater owes you. Take this, with our thanks.
example.dialogue.elder.gift: I brought bread for the village.
example.dialogue.elder.thanks: Bread! The mill has stood idle since the wolves came. Thank you.
example.dialogue.elder.farewell: Walk carefully. The ridge is not kind at night.
example.dialogue.first_wolf.one_down: One down. The rest of the pack won't be far.
example.dialogue.first_wolf.tree_line: Better keep to the tree line.
